Sean Kilpatrick of the Canadian Press reports the public-sector pension board forms joint venture with Nuveen to invest in US shopping centres:

The Public Sector Pension Investment Board has signed a deal to launch a joint venture with Nuveen Real Estate to invest in open-air shopping centres in the United States.The partnership is starting with a US$790-million portfolio.PSP Investments says the strategy is demographically driven, focusing on open-air shopping centres anchored by grocers, necessity-based retailers, and essential services.It is targeting U.S. metro areas with strong population growth, rising household incomes and high barriers to entry, where retailers are seeking to expand.To date, PSP Investments and Nuveen say they have closed deals on 19 assets in Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Minnesota, Texas, California, Colorado, and Washington.PSP Investments invests money for the pension plans of the federal public service, the Canadian Forces, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, and the Reserve Force.

Amit Chowdry of Pulse 2.0 also reports PSP Investments and Nuveen Real Estate launch a $790 million US Retail joint venture:

PSP Investments and Nuveen Real Estate have launched a joint venture with an initial $790 million investment focused on acquiring open-air shopping centers across the United States. The strategy centers on shopping centers anchored by dominant grocers, necessity-based retailers, and essential services. The partners are targeting U.S. metropolitan areas with strong population growth, rising household incomes, and high barriers to new development. To date, the joint venture has acquired 19 properties totaling approximately 3 million square feet across Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Minnesota, Texas, California, Colorado, and Washington. Among the individual acquisitions is The Shoppes of Lorton Valley, a 110,000-square-foot grocery-anchored neighborhood center in Lorton, Virginia. The property is anchored by Giant and serves the broader Washington, D.C. market. The venture has also acquired Las Tiendas Village in Chandler, Arizona, a 188,000-square-foot community shopping center in the Phoenix-Mesa-Chandler metropolitan area. The property is anchored by Sprouts and includes additional national and regional retailers. PSP Investments and Nuveen have also completed two larger portfolio transactions as part of the strategy. One portfolio includes six open-air shopping centers totaling approximately 801,000 square feet across the Fort Lauderdale, San Diego, Orange County, Dallas-Fort Worth, Minneapolis, and Los Angeles markets. A second portfolio consists of 11 properties totaling approximately 1.9 million square feet across California, Colorado, and Washington. The assets are generally positioned near major corridors or high-traffic intersections intended to provide convenient access for daily-needs shoppers. The investment approach reflects a focus on segments of retail real estate that the partners believe can generate relatively durable demand across economic cycles. Grocery-anchored and necessity-based shopping centers have remained a key area of institutional interest because consumers continue to visit them for food, household products, services, and other recurring needs. PSP Investments manages approximately $320.6 billion in net assets, while Nuveen Real Estate manages approximately $135 billion in real estate assets globally. The joint venture combines PSP Investments’ long-term institutional capital with Nuveen’s property sourcing, operating, and asset management capabilities as the partners continue to build their U.S. open-air retail portfolio. KEY QUOTES: “We have been reshaping our U.S. retail exposure around a much tighter definition of the sector: open-air centers anchored by grocers and daily-needs tenants, which aims to deliver a steady, inflation-linked income for our portfolio. Nuveen brings the sourcing reach and operating depth this kind of portfolio demands, and what we own today is exactly the retail exposure our strategy calls for.” Julien Roy-Décary, Managing Director, Real Estate Investments, Americas At PSP Investments “Necessity-based retail has demonstrated remarkable resilience through various cycles, underpinned by consistent consumer demand for essential goods and services. Coupled with PSP Investments’ long-term capital, this venture is designed to deliver both durable income and long-term value creation. We’re confident this combination of scale, relationships, and local execution positions us strongly in one of the most stable and defensive segments of retail real estate.” Brian Wallick, Portfolio Manager, Retail At Nuveen Real Estate

CityBiz also reports PSP Investments and Nuveen Real Estate launch a $790M US Retail Joint Venture:

The Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments) and Nuveen Real Estate have launched a joint venture with $790 million in initial investments to acquire open-air shopping centers across the United States, targeting grocery-anchored properties and retail destinations focused on everyday consumer needs. The partnership has already completed acquisitions totaling approximately 3 million square feet across 19 properties in Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Minnesota, Texas, California, Colorado and Washington. The investments reflect a strategy centered on shopping centers with established grocery tenants, essential services and retailers that generate consistent customer traffic. The joint venture is targeting metropolitan markets with population growth, rising household incomes and significant barriers to new retail development. It is also focusing on locations where established retailers are expanding, creating opportunities for leasing demand and long-term property income. Among the properties acquired is The Shoppes of Lorton Valley, a 110,000-square-foot neighborhood shopping center in Lorton, Virginia, a Washington, D.C., suburb. The property is anchored by Giant, a major grocery operator in the Washington metropolitan area. The venture also acquired Las Tiendas Village, a 188,000-square-foot community shopping center in Chandler, Arizona, within the Phoenix-Mesa-Chandler metropolitan area. The property is anchored by Sprouts, a specialty grocery retailer, and includes additional tenants with established credit profiles. Beyond the individual property acquisitions, PSP Investments and Nuveen have completed two portfolio transactions that expand the venture’s geographic reach. One portfolio includes six open-air shopping centers totaling approximately 801,000 square feet across the Fort Lauderdale, San Diego, Orange County, Dallas-Fort Worth, Minneapolis and Los Angeles markets. A second portfolio comprises 11 properties totaling approximately 1.9 million square feet in California, Colorado and Washington.The properties are located along major commercial corridors or at high-traffic intersections, providing visibility and access for consumers shopping for groceries, household goods and other daily necessities. The investment strategy reflects a more selective approach to retail real estate, emphasizing properties supported by recurring consumer spending rather than discretionary shopping. Grocery-anchored centers have attracted institutional interest because essential retail categories can maintain customer traffic through changing economic conditions. “We have been reshaping our U.S. retail exposure around a much tighter definition of the sector: open-air centers anchored by grocers and daily-needs tenants, which aims to deliver a steady, inflation-linked income for our portfolio,” said Julien Roy-Décary, Managing Director, Real Estate Investments, Americas at PSP Investments. Roy-Décary said Nuveen’s property sourcing capabilities and operating experience complement PSP Investments’ strategy of building a portfolio concentrated in necessity-based retail assets. For Nuveen, the partnership combines its real estate investment and management platform with long-term institutional capital from one of Canada’s largest pension investors. “Necessity-based retail has demonstrated remarkable resilience through various cycles, underpinned by consistent consumer demand for essential goods and services,” said Brian Wallick, Portfolio Manager, Retail at Nuveen Real Estate. Wallick said the venture is structured to pursue recurring income and long-term property value through its investment scale, market relationships and local operating capabilities. The partnership also provides PSP Investments with additional exposure to U.S. retail properties as it manages a diversified global investment portfolio spanning public markets, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, natural resources and credit. Established in 1999, PSP Investments manages pension assets for Canada’s federal Public Service, Canadian Forces, Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Reserve Force. The organization reported $320.6 billion in net assets under management as of March 31, 2026. It is headquartered in Ottawa, with its principal business office in Montréal and additional offices in New York, London and Hong Kong. Nuveen Real Estate manages approximately $135 billion in assets across public and private real estate investments, including debt and equity strategies. The firm has more than 90 years of real estate investment experience and a team of over 590 employees across more than 30 cities in the United States, Europe and Asia Pacific.With its initial 19-property portfolio established, the joint venture gives both investors a sizable position in U.S. open-air retail real estate. Its emphasis on grocery anchors, essential services and growing metropolitan markets is intended to support stable occupancy, recurring rental income and long-term asset performance.

Beyond these individual acquisitions, the joint venture has also completed two larger portfolio acquisitions, adding meaningful scale and geographic diversification, while still maintaining the grocery-anchored and necessity-based thematic focus.
